decisions.text: an outlier inset: East (451) dwarfs the others (at most 16), and the small values must be compared (facts.small_values_matter); the full scale from zero kept, and Central, South, West, North and Others re-plotted on their own scale from zero, 0–20 by 5 (G2.26)
nominal categories sorted by value, descending
last: Others (catch-all, missing, total, then values not known)
every name fits under its bar, neighbours at least 10 pt apart: vertical bars
the unit phrase on the top label: “500 successful transactions”; the top gridline starts after it
the title wraps onto two lines
highlighted in the strong shade of their colour: Central, South; the others keep their colour
the inset inside the plot, in its largest empty area, above the small bars (G2.29, s. 0076)

the inset's form: a frame round the bars of Central, South, West, North and Others, a larger frame round a complete small chart (0–20 by 5, bare numbers (the unit is the main scale's, beside it), the category labels repeated, no title, text at inset size), two links forming a widening cone, beneath the frames (G2.27)
Target (10) as a dotted line in the dark grey across the plot, unlabelled (no free place), named in the inset in bold (D-21 (c), G8.13, G7.16)
Target drawn in the inset too, its value within the inset's range (0–20 by 5), labelled there at the inset's size, the main chart having no place for it (6.6, G8.13)

source.shows: an outlier inset inside the plot: the target line across the main chart, under the inset's frame, and across the inset, where 10 lies in its range (SPEC §6.12.2)
